title: 〜ばこそ
simpleExplanation: 〜ばこそ singles out one reason and says "it is exactly because of this, and for no other reason". It is typically used to explain a behaviour that might look harsh or strange: 厳しく言うのは、あなたを思えばこそだ (I say harsh things precisely because I care about you). The sentence often ends in のだ.
whenUsed: Formal speech and writing. Very common when defending an action driven by good intentions (love, concern, trust). The reason is usually positive; ばこそ is rarely used for negative causes such as laziness or hatred.
formation: Vば + こそ (思えばこそ・あればこそ)
Sentence end: 〜ばこそ、〜のだ / 〜のです

steps.ja: あなたを思うから、厳しく言う
steps.en: I say harsh things because I care (plain reason)

steps.ja: あなたを思えばこそ、厳しく言うのだ
steps.en: it is precisely because I care that I say harsh things (no other reason)

examples.ja: あなたのことを思えばこそ、厳しいことを言うのです。
examples.reading: あなたのことをおもえばこそ、きびしいことをいうのです。
examples.en: It is precisely because I care about you that I say harsh things.
examples.note: Classic defence: harsh words come from care. Note the ending のです.

examples.ja: 健康であればこそ、仕事も趣味も楽しめる。
examples.reading: けんこうであればこそ、しごともしゅみもたのしめる。
examples.en: Precisely because I am healthy, I can enjoy both work and hobbies.
examples.note: 〜であればこそ for a noun/na-adjective: precisely because I am healthy.

examples.ja: 信頼していればこそ、大事な仕事を任せたのだ。
examples.reading: しんらいしていればこそ、だいじなしごとをまかせたのだ。
examples.en: It was precisely because I trusted him that I entrusted him with the important work.
examples.note: 信頼していればこそ: the trust is the sole reason for entrusting the work.

examples.ja: 親であればこそ、子供の将来を心配するのだ。
examples.reading: おやであればこそ、こどものしょうらいをしんぱいするのだ。
examples.en: It is precisely because we are parents that we worry about our children's future.

examples.ja: 苦労があればこそ、成功したときの喜びも大きい。
examples.reading: くろうがあればこそ、せいこうしたときのよろこびもおおきい。
examples.en: Precisely because there is hardship, the joy of success is all the greater.
examples.note: あればこそ is a very common form.

similarGrammar.difference: Also "precisely because", but neutral in register and usable with any reason. ばこそ is more formal and usually a positive reason.
"Only by doing X (does Y hold)": a condition, not a reason. 努力してこそ成功する.
Same ば, but the meaning is "if X happens, it is all over". Unrelated to reasons.

commonMistakes.wrong: 怠けていればこそ、失敗した。
commonMistakes.right: 怠けていたからこそ、失敗した。
commonMistakes.why: ばこそ is normally used for a positive or admirable reason; a negative cause takes からこそ.

commonMistakes.wrong: 愛すればこそ、別れよう。
commonMistakes.right: 愛すればこそ、別れるのだ。
commonMistakes.why: The main clause states a fact or decision with のだ; a volitional ending sounds unnatural.

commonMistakes.wrong: 健康ならこそ、楽しめる。
commonMistakes.right: 健康であればこそ、楽しめる。
commonMistakes.why: Nouns and na-adjectives take であればこそ, not ならこそ.

usageNotes: The main clause usually explains the speaker's own behaviour and ends with のだ / のです.
Typical verbs before it: 思う・愛する・信頼する・大切にする・ある.
It is a favourite in speeches, letters and drama dialogue; everyday talk uses からこそ.
jlptTips: If the sentence defends a harsh or surprising action with a positive reason and ends in のだ, choose ばこそ.
Distractors: からこそ (also correct in meaning, but the ば form in the blank decides), てこそ, ばそれまでだ.
In 並べ替え, the chunk 〜ばこそ usually comes right before the main clause with のだ.
